Solomon — great questions, answered inline below and updated the MAP (v1) to reflect the path-to-dedicated option. Summary:

1) Hosted PoC: we can commit to a PoC SLA (uptime + support response) for the evaluation period in the MAP; data is logically separated per tenant — we’ll include the SLA bullets in the SOW draft.
2) Lift to Dedicated: yes — MAP includes a migration milestone. We propose: PoC on Hosted (2–4 weeks) -> decision gate -> Dedicated onboarding window (2–3 weeks) if you select it. That minimizes risk and keeps early time-to-value.
3) Private / Procurement: estimated procurement + on-prem delivery 8–12 weeks; we’ll put that as an optional lane with longer lead time.

I attached a draft SOW for procurement to review. Confirming kickoff: Tue 2026-09-21 10:30am PT works for us — I’ll send a calendar invite.

See you Tuesday.

—Evelyn

Short bullets as requested:

- Hosted PoC (us-east) feasibility: OK. We can stand up a sandbox Hosted instance and meet perf target for 1–2 teams with the following caveats: sequence lengths and concurrency shape matter; I recommend the PoC use sample production prompts + a 5% traffic ramp.
- Migration path to Dedicated: typical cutover flow = 1) capacity reservation + smoke test (1–2 business days), 2) data sync for KV/prefix caches (hours), 3) DNS flip and canary traffic (1–2 days). Plan on 2–3 full business days for standard workloads.
- Private (on-prem): procurement and infra prep ~8–12 weeks depending on customer infra readiness; we will need VPN/KMS requirements up front.
- Risk: if opalia requires EU geo for initial PoC, we need to schedule capacity checks earlier; US east default minimizes procurement friction.

I will prepare a 1-page migration checklist to attach to the MAP before the kickoff.

—Karthik
